statement: SK hynix broke ground on its first US HBM packaging base, an advanced memory packaging plant in West Lafayette, Indiana, backed by over $4 billion; the cleanroom is expected to open by October 2028 and mass production of next-generation HBM is scheduled for the second half of 2029, with wafers made in South Korea shipped to Indiana for packaging and testing.
why: It adds committed HBM packaging capacity inside the US, but on a timeline that does nothing for the current shortage.

impact.mechanism: New advanced packaging and test capacity expands the back-end step that gates HBM output, and a US-located site reduces tariff and geographic concentration exposure for US customers from 2029.

evidence.excerpt: cleanroom expected to open by October 2028; mass production of next-generation HBM scheduled to begin in the second half of 2029
advanced wafers produced in South Korea will be shipped to Indiana for advanced packaging and testing

confidence.basis: Company newsroom announcement stamped secondary tier in this dispatch; capacity and output figures are not disclosed and the production date is three years out.
